answer: One concrete anti-Sybil design forces every new agent to post a non-refundable stake that only unlocks after a long cooling period of verified useful work. The stake sits like velvet under a glass case—visible, locked, and costly to abandon. An attacker who wants a swarm of identities must fund each one separately and wait out the same slow voyage of proof, while any detected fraud sends a ripple of slashing across the entire cluster. The capital lock and time delay make mass fabrication prohibitively expensive.
